The five phases, and what they cost

Where the frame budget goes

phasewhat happensruns onblocks the main thread?
JavaScriptyou change the DOM or a styleCPUyes
Stylere-match selectors, rebuild the subtreeCPUyes
Layoutrecompute position and size of every affected boxCPUyes
Paintrecord the draw commands, then rasterise them into bitmapsCPU → GPUthe recording does
Compositestack the bitmaps in the right orderGPUno
~16ms per frame. Style and Layout spend it — and you can avoid both.

DOM architecture

Why methods live where they do

Query methods sit on Element.prototype, not HTMLElement — so <svg> and XML nodes get the same API.
MODULE 02 · VIDEO 2

Query cost

Live collections turn loops quadratic

The trap · a live HTMLCollection

// getElementsByClassName returns a LIVE collection!
const cards = document.getElementsByClassName('card');

for (let i = 0; i < cards.length; i++) {
  // Every read re-verifies tree position! Total: O(N²)
  process(cards[i]);
}

Fix: querySelectorAll, or snapshot with Array.from().

What each one costs

MethodComplexityReturn Type
getElementByIdO(1)hashmap lookup
getElementsByClassNameO(N) per readlive HTMLCollection
querySelectorAllO(1) per readstatic NodeList
Scope the query: grid.querySelectorAll('.row') searches twelve nodes, document searches ten thousand.
MODULE 02 · VIDEO 2
07 / 23
Mutation

A hundred mutations, one reflow

Why not innerHTML +=

It destroys the existing children and their listeners, runs the HTML tokenizer, and forces a full reflow.

Build in memory, append once

// 1. Clone lightweight fragment from <template>
const clone = template.content.cloneNode(true);
const card = clone.firstElementChild;

// 2. Mutate in memory — ZERO layout pass!
card.querySelector('.title').textContent = datum.title;

// 3. Exactly ONE reflow pass on final append:
container.appendChild(clone);
A <template> is outside the render tree. Mutating it never wakes layout.

The tree nobody shows you in DevTools by default

One document, two trees

<button> arrives with a role, a name, a focus stop and keyboard behaviour. <div> arrives with none of it.
MODULE 02 · VIDEO 3
09 / 23
The same widget, twice

What the element was already doing for you

// the version that ships in most codebases
<div class="btn" onclick="save()">
  Save
</div>
No role. No name in the tree. Not in the tab order. Enter and Space do nothing. Voice control cannot address it.
// the version that needs no JavaScript at all
<button type="button" onclick="save()">
  Save
</button>
Role button, accessible name "Save", a focus stop, Enter and Space fire click, and :disabled stops the event instead of just greying it.

Say this in the interview

Role, name, state

Role

What is this?

From the tag — or a role that overrides it.

Breaks when a <div> is the control.

Name

What is it called?

From content, <label>, aria-label.

Breaks on icon-only buttons.

State

What is it doing?

From disabled, checked, aria-expanded.

Breaks when the state is a CSS class.

"The tag is the call, the accessibility tree is the return value — and <button> returns all three for free."

Why z-index: 9999 did nothing

z-index is local, not global

<header style="opacity:.99">   // ← creates a context
  ...
</header>

<div class="dropdown" style="z-index:9999">
  // still paints under the header
</div>
9999 only ranks the element against its siblings inside its own stacking context. It can never lift it out of that context.
header · z-index 2
dropdown · z-index 9999

The second hierarchy

The containing block decides what percentages mean

ElementIts containing block isThe trap
position: static / relativeThe content box of the nearest block ancestorPercentage heights collapse when the parent has no height
position: absoluteThe padding box of the nearest positioned ancestorForget position:relative on the parent and it escapes to the page
position: fixedThe viewport — unless an ancestor has transform, filter, perspective, contain or will-changeA CSS animation on a wrapper silently un-fixes every fixed child inside it
The bug that looks like a browser bug: a fixed modal that scrolls away, because a parent has transform on it.
MODULE 02 · VIDEO 5
16 / 23
Forced synchronous layout · the loop that costs 60 reflows

Read, write, read — and the frame dies

// 60 elements → 60 forced layouts
boxes.forEach(el => {
  const w = el.offsetWidth;   // read → flush
  el.style.width = w + 10 + 'px'; // write
})
Each write invalidates layout, so the next read forces a full recompute — once per element.
// 60 elements → 1 layout
const widths = boxes.map(el => el.offsetWidth); // read all
boxes.forEach((el, i) =>
  el.style.width = widths[i] + 10 + 'px')   // write all
Same result, one reflow. Read all, then write all.
400 real divs, measured on this machine.
Forces the flush: offsetWidth, clientWidth, scrollTop, getBoundingClientRect(), getComputedStyle(), focus().

MODULE 02 · VIDEO 5

The judgement call

Promote a widget. Never promote a page.

Worth a layer

One element that moves constantly: a drag handle, a sticky header, a video, an open modal.

Not worth a layer

Every row of a list. Anything static. Anything promoted "just in case".

CPU where the GPU would do drops frames fast. GPU everywhere runs out of memory slowly. Prefer the GPU — count the layers.

One stack, two queues, one rule

Microtasks drain completely; tasks take one at a time

One task, then the entire microtask queue — including microtasks queued by microtasks. Only then may the browser render.
MODULE 02 · VIDEO 6
21 / 23
The frame you just missed

16.7ms, and your task took 80

The long task

Sorting 20,000 rows blocks the render step: no paint, no click handled. The page is frozen, not slow. Over 50ms is a long task.

The three ways out

Chunk it — yield with scheduler.yield(). Move it — a Web Worker. Skip it — virtualize.

"A frame only happens between tasks. An 80ms handler is three dropped frames, and the fix is a shorter task, not a faster loop."
